issues.description: The problem statement's UML specifies Ride.abbreviation as type 'char' (Ride -abbreviation: char) but the solution's Ride class declares the abbreviation attribute and constructor parameter as String. This is an attribute type mismatch: students reading the UML expect a char but the reference implementation uses String. This inconsistency will confuse students about the correct type to implement for the abbreviation attribute and its getter/constructor parameter.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the abbreviation type consistent across artifacts. Preferably update the solution (and template) so Ride.abbreviation is of type char and the constructor and getter use char (matching the UML/problem). Alternatively, if String is intended, update the problem statement UML and any textual description to state abbreviation: String.

issues.description: There is an internal constructor parameter mismatch in the solution: RollerCoaster and subclasses use a constructor parameter of type 'char' for abbreviation, but Ride's constructor in the solution expects a String. In the solution, RollerCoaster's constructor calls super(name, abbreviation) passing a char to Ride's constructor that expects a String. This inconsistency will cause compilation errors and prevents students from following the reference implementation or using it as a template.
issues.suggested_fix: Ensure constructor parameter types match the superclass signature. If abbreviation should be a char per the UML, change Ride's constructor and attribute to use char (and update its getter). If abbreviation should be a String, update RollerCoaster and all subclasses to accept and forward a String instead of a char. Make the change consistently in both template and solution.

issues.description: The UML problem statement declares the Ride attribute 'abbreviation' as type char, but the solution implementation declares Ride.abbreviation as a String (Ride.java) while several subclass constructors (RollerCoaster, LaunchedRollerCoaster, LaunchedDropdownTower) expect a char parameter for abbreviation. This creates a cross-artifact representation mismatch for the same conceptual entity 'abbreviation' (attribute and constructor parameter). Students will be confused which type to use when implementing constructors/getters and the mismatch can cause compilation errors when calling super(...) across classes. The inconsistency prevents a clear 1:1 mapping from the UML specification to the provided solution code.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the 'abbreviation' representation consistent across all artifacts. Two possible fixes (choose one consistently):
1) Align implementation with the UML: change Ride.abbreviation to type char (private char abbreviation; constructor public Ride(String name, char abbreviation); getter public char getAbbreviation()), and update all subclass constructors and super(...) calls to use char. OR
2) Update the UML/problem statement to specify abbreviation: String, and ensure all constructors and attributes in solution and template use String consistently. Prefer option (1) to follow the original UML, unless there is an intentional reason to use String.
